subject.title: [TUI] Scroll-jump / auto-scroll behavior is still disruptive in 2026.3.8

question: Should this broad TUI scroll-jump tracker be solved by a TUI auto-follow setting, a renderer/dependency scrollback fix, or by landing the narrower renderer fix first and then revisiting the broader UX request?
rationale: The source path and related issue evidence are credible, but the solution shape crosses default TUI behavior, possible settings surface, and third-party renderer ownership, so automation should not choose the product direction alone.

options.title: Coordinate setting plus renderer repair
options.body: Keep this broad tracker open, land or upstream the renderer scrollback fix, then add TUI-owned follow semantics only if live proof still shows disruptive auto-scroll.

options.title: Add TUI follow mode now
options.body: Add a visible TUI near-bottom/off/always-style control with PTY proof, accepting the new UX surface and keeping it separate from WebChat settings.

options.title: Narrow to renderer fix only
options.body: Treat the remaining actionable work as the renderer scrollback-clearing issue and avoid adding a user-facing TUI auto-scroll setting unless fresh proof demands it.

recommendation.title: Coordinate setting plus renderer repair
recommendation.body: Keep this broad tracker open, land or upstream the renderer scrollback fix, then add TUI-owned follow semantics only if live proof still shows disruptive auto-scroll.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest product-shape and current TUI snapshot routing signal for deciding between renderer repair and new TUI UX surface.
